references.text: A bull from the herd is mentioned as a burnt offering to the Lord, corresponding to the young bull in the Levites' consecration ceremony.
The grain offering (mincha) of fine flour mixed with oil is described here, corresponding to the same offering that was to accompany the bull in Numbers 8:8.
A young bull as a sin offering is mentioned, corresponding to the second bull that was to be taken as a sin offering for the Levites.
A young bull as a sin offering for the whole congregation, parallel to the sin offering for the cleansing of the Levites.
Describes the grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil that is to accompany a young bull, the same combination as in the consecration of the Levites.
Three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering for each bull, corresponding to the offering pattern in 8:8.
At the consecration of the priests, a young bull and unleavened bread mixed with oil were also to be used, parallel to the Levites' consecration ceremony.
The Epistle to the Hebrews refers to bulls and goats as sin offerings under the old covenant, pointing to Christ's blood as the perfect offering that replaces these.
